recipes.name: Run 1
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side
Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 76.35 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 8.15 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, down to 0.50 in along the point. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 75.60 in along the point; 67.79 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 60.31 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the sawn face that lies on the open side -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a square-ended block 3.55 in long. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 75.60 in along the point, 67.79 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, 60.31 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
42 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece, flipped, lies flat on the frame's 45° slope: sawn face on sawn face, a full-width bearing.
Every other seam is sawn-to-sawn (tight, full face); the ones between are bark-to-bark, touching on a line, with a lens of air either side.
2 pieces near the corners are under 6 in long: cut them from offcuts.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.
